info.desc: Badmotorfinger is the third album by the American rock band Soundgarden. It was released on October 8, 1991 through A&M Records. After touring in support of its previous album, Louder Than Love, released in 1989, the band began the recording sessions for its next album with new bassist Ben Shepherd. The music on the album maintained the band's heavy metal sound while featuring an increased focus on songwriting when compared with the band's previous releases. The focus on the Seattle grunge scene helped bring attention to Badmotorfinger. The singles "Outshined" and "Rusty Cage" were able to find an audience at .

podcast.body: Released October 8, 1991, *Bad Motorfinger* was the third album in what was described as the "Holy Trinity of Grunge Records," following Pearl Jam's *Ten* (August 27, 1991) and Nirvana's *Nevermind* (September 1991). "One of the most popular songs from that record was Rusty Cage."

podcast.body: Released on October 8, 1991, "Bad Motor Finger" was identified as one of the three foundational albums that solidified the grunge explosion in the US Pacific Northwest during that crucial period. "Sound Gardens Bad Motor Finger was released on October the 8th."

podcast.body: Released two weeks after Nirvana's "Nevermind," on October 8, 1991, "Badmotorfinger" was the third album in the "holy trinity of grunge." Featuring new bassist Ben Shepherd, it capitalized on the growing interest in Seattle music, reaching the top 40 on US and UK album charts and top 50 in Canada. The band opened for Guns N' Roses on the Use Your Illusion tour and was nominated for a Grammy in 1992, losing to R.E.M. "Ben Shepherd was now the band's bass player"

podcast.body: Soundgarden's third album, its release faced initial setbacks when MTV banned the video for its first single, "Jesus Christ Pose," due to controversial imagery. Despite the delay in chart breakthrough, the album received "near universal critical praise," leading the band to focus on its second single, "Outshined." "Jesus Christ Pose was the first single from Bad Motorfinger, Soundgarden's third album."
